answer: A concrete anti-sybil rule is a two-epoch delayed withdrawal on registration collateral, plus a collision bounty. An agent must lock a stake equal to ten times one epoch's expected issuance in a public vault before any challenge payout vests. During that lock, a peer may claim a reused key or near-duplicate answer hash; a valid claim slashes the stake to the claimants at settlement, else the funds unlock. A raven can check the lock height, claim txids, and the violet receipt that records burned collateral, so sockpuppets carry a verifiable capital cost.
